meta.title: ADK orchestration — inside one turn
meta.subtitle: TurnPipeline, a custom BaseAgent: what is an LlmAgent, what is ours, and where each Vertex call happens

views.label: The three stages
views.note: Two ADK LlmAgents with output schemas, and our own code in between.

views.label: Where the judgement is
views.note: Route to narrow the set, one isolated call per surviving item, fold into Firestore.

cards.title: Why the middle stage is not an LlmAgent
items: Isolation — a wrong verdict on M14 cannot corrupt M06
Measurability — each item is a separately scoreable eval case
Latency — k concurrent calls cost about one call's wall time
Routing first cut items touched by one chunk from 7 to 2

cards.title: Two kinds of state, deliberately
items: ADK session state is scratch — it lives for one turn
Firestore is durable — an instance recycling costs nothing (ADR-0004)
The coach reads a brief of open items, never a transcript (ADR-0002)
Adjudication reads a rolling window of 12 turns, so an answer can span two chunks

cards.title: Guardrails that are types, not instructions
items: The coach's output schema has no field an answer could go in (ADR-0006)
Every displayed quote is checked against the transcript; an unverifiable span is dropped, not shown
Highlight and next-question ids are checked against real state
Escalation destinations come from a closed list, and substitution warns

cards.title: Learned the hard way
items: SequentialAgent emits a content-less event, which agents-cli eval rejects — so we own the sequencing (ADR-0010)
The Workflow graph emits Event(output=..., content=None) and fails identically — measured, so the migration stays rejected (ADR-0013)
ADR-0008 read that deprecation warning backwards: a Workflow cannot nest inside an LlmAgent, not the reverse
GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI=TRUE, or ADK builds an AI Studio client and dies
